title: Dhanush Says No One but Sai Pallavi Could Have Played Sita in Ramayana
excerpt: At the OM pre-release event on November 7, Dhanush dismissed the noise around Sai Pallavi's casting as Sita, pointing to her devotion and calling her a great performer.
body:
• Dhanush publicly defended Sai Pallavi's casting as Sita in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana at the pre-release event for their film OM on Saturday, November 7.
  • He said he does not understand the noise around her portrayal, pointing to her devotion — praying even during shot breaks — and calling her a great performer.
  • Ramayana: Part 1, the Hindi-language epic starring Ranbir Kapoor as Rama and Yash as Ravana, released in theatres on November 5.
  • Dhanush and Sai Pallavi next appear together in OM: Chapter 1, releasing November 20, in which she plays CBI officer Nithya Reddy.

Actor Dhanush has come out firmly behind Sai Pallavi's portrayal of Sita in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana, dismissing the criticism that has followed her casting. Speaking at a pre-release event in Chennai on Saturday, November 7, for their upcoming film OM, Dhanush said no one else could have done justice to the role, according to reports of the event.

"There is so much noise around her portrayal of Sita. I don't understand it. Even during shot breaks, she would be praying constantly. She is someone with such profound devotion to God, someone with such a pure heart. She looks so beautiful and she is a great performer."

— Dhanush, at the OM pre-release event

Why Dhanush says the casting works

Dhanush's argument rests on what he has seen of Sai Pallavi off camera as much as on it. He highlighted her personal commitment to her craft and her spiritual nature, saying her performance is rooted in both professional skill and a genuine, pure-hearted approach to the character. Pinkvilla reported that Dhanush also said he had watched her journey from its early stages and witnessed her transformation into an accomplished actress who had mastered the art of cinema — and that, addressing the speculation about her playing Sita, he felt she was the perfect choice for the role.

The film at the centre of the debate

Ramayana is a Hindi-language adaptation of Valmiki's epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Prime Focus Studios in association with DNEG and Monster Mind Creations. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama opposite Sai Pallavi's Sita, with Yash as Ravana, Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. Part 1 released in theatres on Thursday, November 5, and early reviews have singled out Yash's Ravana while describing Sai Pallavi's Sita as graceful, with poise and dignity. Dhanush is not her only defender among the cast: Ranbir Kapoor had earlier recalled that when he first saw her as Sita on set, he and Tiwari both knew they could not have cast someone better.

Why he was speaking: OM

The remarks came at the pre-release event for OM: Chapter 1 — Udhiram: The Blood Wood, an action drama directed by Rajkumar Periasamy that reunites Dhanush and Sai Pallavi and is slated for release on November 20, 2026. In the film, Sai Pallavi plays CBI officer Nithya Reddy, who investigates the illegal red sandalwood trade — a role Dhanush commended her for taking on with bravery and poise. He also framed the film itself expansively: "OM: Chapter 1 has five heroes. Mammootty sir, Sai Pallavi, Sreeleela, Sai Abhyankkar, and then only me. It's not a multi-starrer; it's a multi-hero film." Mammootty, for his part, praised Sai Pallavi's "flickering expressions" at the same event. The film also features Naseeruddin Shah in a pivotal role, with music by Sai Abhyankkar, and is planned as the first instalment of a two-part franchise.

What diaspora viewers need to know

For Indian audiences abroad, the practical picture is simple: Ramayana: Part 1 is in theatres now, and the Sita debate is the conversation around it — one of the film's most prominent peers has now answered it on the record. OM: Chapter 1 follows on November 20 for viewers who want to see Dhanush and Sai Pallavi together in a contemporary action role.
